pencereler.0-5: Twelve people died that night. A bulk carrier crashed into the piers of Hobart's
pencereler.5-12: Tasman Bridge. Two spans fell onto the ship, and it sank. The current had pushed it off course. It
pencereler.12-20: struck piers that were never meant to face a ship. In the dark, cars drove into the gap. The city was split
pencereler.20-30: in two for years. Ships and traffic were then kept apart whenever vessels passed.

bulgular: 12-20s: no central mystery or problem is posed

segmentler.metin: The Tasman Bridge lost spans when a bulk carrier hit its piers.
It took only a bulk carrier pushed off course by the current.
So how could a bulk carrier pushed off course by the current do this?
The answer is ship impact on unprotected piers outside the navigation span — and it is why shipping rules around the bridge were tightened and traffic was stopped for passing ships.
